title: Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing

spark.summary: A Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway unifies heterogeneous model providers behind one OpenAI-compatible API, routing each prompt by semantic complexity, cost budget, and real-time EWMA provider health.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, route 70% of simple prompts to fast, low-cost models via a sub-10ms complexity classifier, while protecting tail latency with EWMA health scoring, hedged fallbacks, and token-bucket TPM/RPM limits.
spark.byteSummary:
Sending every enterprise LLM request to a single frontier reasoning model wastes 5x-15x in inference cost and exposes applications to single-provider 429 rate limits and regional outages. A Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway acts as an intelligent Layer-7 control plane between internal services and upstream model endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, and self-hosted vLLM clusters).

On every request, the gateway authenticates the tenant, enforces dual token-bucket limits (Requests-Per-Minute and estimated Tokens-Per-Minute), checks a Redis Vector semantic cache, and runs a lightweight (<10ms) complexity classifier. Simple classification, extraction, or summarization prompts route to Tier-1 fast models (e.g., Haiku / Llama-8B), while multi-step reasoning or code synthesis routes to Tier-2 frontier models.

To survive upstream instability, the gateway maintains sliding-window EWMA (Exponentially Weighted Moving Average) scores for Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and 5xx/429 error rates per provider. Circuit breakers trip unhealthy upstreams automatically, while hedged speculative retries and unified SSE stream adapters keep downstream clients completely insulated from provider schema differences.

learningJourney.title: Unified Schema Translation & SSE Stream Normalization
learningJourney.purpose: Expose one OpenAI-compatible contract while adapting payloads across diverse model providers.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Unified Schema Translation & SSE Stream Normalization** as the intuition layer for Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing: Expose one OpenAI-compatible contract while adapting payloads across diverse model providers.
explanation.core: Different providers use incompatible wire formats (`messages` vs `contents`, `system` top-level field vs system role, different SSE event shapes and finish reasons). The Gateway Adapter translates incoming requests into canonical IR, dispatches to the selected provider's native client, and normalizes streaming deltas, tool calls, and token usage counts back into a single unified SSE schema.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, unified schema translation & sse stream normalization becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize tail latency and quality assurance with pre-token hedged retries, 1% shadow evaluations, and FinOps Kafka-ClickHouse ledgers.

learningJourney.title: Dual Token-Bucket TPM & RPM Rate Limiting
learningJourney.purpose: Enforce both request-rate and token-volume fairness across multi-tenant workloads.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Dual Token-Bucket TPM & RPM Rate Limiting** as the intuition layer for Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing: Enforce both request-rate and token-volume fairness across multi-tenant workloads.
explanation.core: Standard API gateways only count Requests-Per-Minute (RPM), which fails for LLMs because a single 100K-token prompt consumes 1,000x more GPU compute than a 100-token query. The LLM Gateway runs atomic Redis Lua scripts implementing dual token buckets: pre-deducting estimated input tokens + `max_tokens` before upstream dispatch, then reconciling actual `usage` tokens once the stream completes.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, dual token-bucket tpm & rpm rate limiting becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize tail latency and quality assurance with pre-token hedged retries, 1% shadow evaluations, and FinOps Kafka-ClickHouse ledgers.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, route 70% of simple prompts to fast, low-cost models via a sub-10ms complexity classifier, while protecting tail latency with EWMA health scoring, hedged fallbacks, and token-bucket TPM/RPM limits.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Semantic Complexity Classification & Cost-Aware Routing
learningJourney.purpose: Route simple prompts to 10x cheaper fast models without degrading hard-task accuracy.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Semantic Complexity Classification & Cost-Aware Routing** as the intuition layer for Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing: Route simple prompts to 10x cheaper fast models without degrading hard-task accuracy.
explanation.core: A lightweight BERT/ModernBERT router or embedding similarity classifier (~5-8ms on CPU/ONNX) scores incoming prompt complexity along dimensions like reasoning depth, code synthesis, and ambiguity. Combined with tenant SLA headers (`x-routing-policy: cost-optimized | quality-first`), Tier-1 prompts route to small fast models ($0.10/1M tokens) while Tier-2 prompts route to frontier models ($5-$15/1M tokens).
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, semantic complexity classification & cost-aware routing becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize tail latency and quality assurance with pre-token hedged retries, 1% shadow evaluations, and FinOps Kafka-ClickHouse ledgers.

learningJourney.title: EWMA Health Scoring, Circuit Breakers & Fallback Chains
learningJourney.purpose: Detect degraded providers in seconds and fail over automatically before timeouts cascade.

explanation.foundation: Static round-robin keeps sending traffic to a provider experiencing 500ms+ TTFT or 20% 429s.
explanation.core: The gateway tracks per-model EWMA TTFT and error rates over 10-second windows.
explanation.deepDive: When a provider crosses the error threshold (e.g., >10% 5xx/429s), its circuit breaker opens for 30s and traffic shifts immediately to the next model in the tenant's fallback chain (e.g., Anthropic -> Bedrock -> Azure OpenAI).

cards.label: Same-Family Fallback

sectionDiagram.summary: EWMA health scoring and circuit breakers insulate apps from single-provider brownouts.
sectionDiagram.caption: Half-open canary probing prevents thundering herds when an upstream recovers.

learningJourney.title: Semantic Cache & Prompt-Aware Deduplication
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate redundant LLM calls for recurring FAQ, classification, and support queries.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Semantic Cache & Prompt-Aware Deduplication** as the intuition layer for Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing: Eliminate redundant LLM calls for recurring FAQ, classification, and support queries.
explanation.core: Before invoking any upstream model, the gateway computes a fast embedding of the normalized prompt (plus system-prompt hash) and queries a Redis Vector / Qdrant index. If cosine similarity exceeds 0.96 (and temperature <= 0.2), the cached response streams back immediately in <25ms at zero token cost—while skipping cache for high-temperature creative or user-PII-bearing requests.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, semantic cache & prompt-aware deduplication becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize tail latency and quality assurance with pre-token hedged retries, 1% shadow evaluations, and FinOps Kafka-ClickHouse ledgers.

learningJourney.title: Hedged Speculative Retries & Tail-Latency Clipping
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate p99 pre-token stalls without doubling total inference spend.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Hedged Speculative Retries & Tail-Latency Clipping** as the intuition layer for Dynamic Multi-Model LLM Gateway & Smart Routing: Eliminate p99 pre-token stalls without doubling total inference spend.
explanation.core: If an upstream provider accepts a TCP connection but stalls before sending token 1 (p99 tail spike), waiting for a 30-second timeout ruins UX. For idempotent, non-mutating requests, if TTFT exceeds the p95 threshold (e.g., 1.2s) with no bytes received, the gateway fires a hedged request to a secondary provider, streams whichever yields token 1 first, and cancels the slower socket.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, hedged speculative retries & tail-latency clipping becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Optimize tail latency and quality assurance with pre-token hedged retries, 1% shadow evaluations, and FinOps Kafka-ClickHouse ledgers.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does an LLM Gateway need dual TPM (Tokens-Per-Minute) and RPM (Requests-Per-Minute) token buckets with post-stream reconciliation?

options.text: Because a single 100K-token prompt consumes orders of magnitude more GPU compute and provider quota than a 100-token prompt.
options.feedback: Correct! Request counts alone cannot protect against massive-context bursts; pre-reserving estimated tokens and refunding unused max_tokens keeps TPM accurate.

options.text: Because Redis Lua scripts cannot count integer requests.
options.feedback: Redis Lua easily counts both requests and tokens atomically.

options.text: To disable SSE streaming for large prompts.
options.feedback: Rate limiting works seamlessly with SSE streaming.

options.text: Because OpenAI and Anthropic use the same wire format.
options.feedback: Wire format differences are handled by protocol adapters, not rate limiters.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: LLM cost and GPU capacity scale with token volume, not just HTTP request count. Dual RPM/TPM buckets with pre-reservation and post-stream reconciliation prevent noisy-neighbor exhaustion.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under what condition is it safe for an LLM Gateway to fire a hedged speculative retry to a secondary provider?

options.text: After 500 tokens have already been streamed to the user.
options.feedback: Hedging after streaming begins would cause duplicate or conflicting text in the user's UI.

options.text: Only before token 1 is received/flushed, when TTFT exceeds the p95 threshold and total hedge rate is capped (<5%).
options.feedback: Correct! Pre-token hedging clips tail TTFT spikes cleanly, and capping hedge volume prevents amplifying upstream outages.

options.text: Whenever the user sends a high-temperature creative prompt.
options.feedback: Temperature does not determine when to hedge; TTFT stalls do.

options.text: Only when the semantic cache hits.
options.feedback: Semantic cache hits return in <25ms without calling any upstream provider.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Hedged requests must fire only before the first token is sent downstream, and must be capped during widespread outages to avoid retry storms.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a semantic vector cache key be scoped in a multi-tenant LLM Gateway?

options.text: By raw user prompt text alone across all tenants.
options.feedback: Sharing raw prompt caches across tenants risks leaking confidential responses and ignoring differing system prompts.

options.text: Partitioned by tenant_id + system_prompt_hash + model_tier, and bypassed for high-temperature or PII-flagged requests.
options.feedback: Correct! Tenant and system-prompt scoping prevents cross-tenant data leaks and stale behavioral mismatches.
IP addresses change and do not capture tenant or system-prompt boundaries.
User-Agent has nothing to do with semantic prompt equivalence.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Multi-tenant semantic caches must strictly isolate namespaces by tenant_id and system_prompt_hash to prevent cross-tenant data leakage.

beginner.summary: Learn how an LLM Gateway routes prompts across multiple AI providers to save money and stay online during outages.
beginner.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, route 70% of simple prompts to fast, low-cost models via a sub-10ms complexity classifier, while protecting tail latency with EWMA health scoring, hedged fallbacks, and token-bucket TPM/RPM limits.
beginner.byteSummary:
Instead of hardcoding a single AI provider into your app, an LLM Gateway gives all your services one unified endpoint. It translates requests for OpenAI, Anthropic, or self-hosted models automatically.

A fast classifier checks each prompt: simple tasks go to low-cost models, while complex reasoning goes to frontier models. If a provider has an outage, the gateway routes around it automatically.

intermediate.summary: Build a multi-model gateway with OpenAI-compatible SSE adapters, dual RPM/TPM Redis Lua limiters, and EWMA circuit breakers.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, route 70% of simple prompts to fast, low-cost models via a sub-10ms complexity classifier, while protecting tail latency with EWMA health scoring, hedged fallbacks, and token-bucket TPM/RPM limits.
intermediate.byteSummary:
An enterprise LLM Gateway normalizes heterogeneous provider APIs into a single SSE contract while enforcing dual RPM and TPM token buckets via atomic Redis Lua scripts. A tenant-isolated Redis Vector cache serves recurring low-temperature queries in <25ms.

For cache misses, a sub-10ms ONNX classifier splits traffic between Tier-1 fast models and Tier-2 frontier models, while EWMA TTFT/error-rate circuit breakers trigger automatic cross-cloud failovers.

advanced.summary: Optimize tail latency and quality assurance with pre-token hedged retries, 1% shadow evaluations, and FinOps Kafka-ClickHouse ledgers.
advanced.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, route 70% of simple prompts to fast, low-cost models via a sub-10ms complexity classifier, while protecting tail latency with EWMA health scoring, hedged fallbacks, and token-bucket TPM/RPM limits.
advanced.byteSummary:
At 50K+ RPS, p99 pre-token stalls are mitigated using TTFT-watchdog hedged retries capped at <5% traffic volume so retries never amplify provider brownouts. The winning stream flushes immediately while the losing socket aborts.

Quality regression is monitored asynchronously by mirroring 1% of Tier-1 routed prompts to frontier judges, feeding win-rate telemetry alongside real-time Kafka-to-ClickHouse FinOps chargeback ledgers.
